newsitem.title: GERMANY: Former German leader calls on Kohl, Waigel to quit.
newsitem.headline: Former German leader calls on Kohl, Waigel to quit.

text.p: Former German chancellor Helmut Schmidt on Monday called on his successor Helmut Kohl and Finance Minister Theo Waigel to resign over what he said was the government's fiscal mismanagement.
Speaking to ARD television, Schmidt said he saw no way for Waigel to lead Germany out of its current fiscal troubles and that Waigel himself was chiefly to blame.

"The only thing left to do is to make room for people with new ideas," said Schmidt, a Social Democrat who governed from 1974 to 1982 when the junior partner in his coalition, the Free Democrats, defected to the Christian Democrats, bringing Kohl to power.
"And that is even more applicable for his government chief."
Schmidt said Waigel had been "entirely unprofessional and a dilettante" for demanding strict criteria in the Maastricht Treaty for monetary union and then trying to fudge them.
The sharp criticism of Waigel followed a report in the Hamburger Morgenpost newspaper that Waigel met Schmidt in Hamburg, Schmidt's hometown. Schmidt's office in Bonn confirmed the meeting.

The Moregenpost said Waigel asked Schmidt to mediate the possible formation of a grand coalition between the Social Democrats (SPD) and the conservative Christian Democrats and Christian Social Union (CDU/CSU) in the event Kohl's centre-right coalition with the liberal Free Democrats (FDP) collapses.
A spokesman at Schmidt's office declined to comment on the substance of the meeting.
A separate report in the newspaper Die Welt said the CDU/CSU viewed Schmidt as a key contact in the SPD that Kohl's coalition was eager to maintain in face of FDP threats to leave the coalition.
Bavaria state finance minister Erwin Huber of the CSU told Southwest German radio that Waigel and Schmidt were not talking about a grand coalition.
Huber said Waigel and Schmidt, who himself was finance minister before becoming chancellor in 1974, had merely stayed in contact over the years.
